hypothesis: A five-state decoder-visible XML lexical state partitions endpoint residual calibration strongly enough to save at least 2100 bytes per million raw bytes on chronological holdout without changing the WRT trajectory.
interfaces_exposed: five-state decoded-raw XML lexical state to WRT-bit endpoint residual calibration
kill_condition: Retire this realization if exact chronological holdout is non-positive; classify 0 to 600 B/M as negligible and 600 to 2100 B/M as complementary only.
promotion_condition: Select the blend on development only; promote if exact chronological holdout saves at least 2100 B/M, remains positive globally, and later survives a disjoint offset gate with complete source accounting.
rejection_reason: Exact same-coder chronological holdout lost 8 bytes (-43.5718 B/M); the XML-state coordinate was 1 byte worse than the matched state-blind calibration control. Retire unchanged with zero score credit.
retired_neighborhoods: Unlike retired page-global endpoint calibration and negative Wheeler retrieval shadows, this tests a per-bit causal lexical state with no page label, retrieval index, reordering, or PPM parameter sweep.
title: ACS Prover XML lexical-state endpoint calibration
